summary:
The Sakha Republic stands under the national framework of Russia, and no Sakha-specific legislation on gender identity or sexual orientation was identified. The republic falls within the reach of the national extremism designation of the "international LGBT public movement", which bars organising, symbols and support; the designation applies in the republic as it does nationally.

The one documented Sakha-specific enforcement action is custodial. In November 2024 a court in Yakutsk imposed an additional sentence on a prisoner for allegedly showing the rainbow flag to other prisoners. The ruling shows the national ban on the movement's symbols being enforced inside the republic's penal system, against a person already in state custody.

No Sakha-specific protection machinery was identified. The sources reviewed record no regional anti-discrimination provision and no regional body that recognises trans identity or registers LGBTQ organisations. A trans visitor to the republic should expect the national regime to apply without regional mitigation.
tangentialFactors: The Sakha Republic appears in the sources as one of the sub-national units covered by the national extremism designation, with enforcement running through national statutes rather than any regional instrument. The sources reviewed identify no regional policy divergence from the national framework and offer no comparison with other Russian regions.
localsOnly: Residents of the Sakha Republic face the national prohibitions without a regional layer of protection. The documented local enforcement is custodial: a Yakutsk court added a sentence in November 2024 for showing the rainbow flag to other prisoners. Organising, funding or joining the designated movement is barred under the national extremism designation, and the sources reviewed record no Sakha-specific registration route or protection body.
outOfScopeNotes: The sources reviewed do not record the length of the additional sentence imposed in Yakutsk in November 2024, the charge under which it was imposed, or whether the flag display was the sole ground. No Sakha-specific figures on hate crimes, prosecutions under the propaganda statutes, or violence against trans people were identified. Whether the republic's police and courts apply the national statutes outside the penal system in any distinctive way is not established by the sources reviewed.
